compareCandidate.label: Equivalent vs. equal-looking
compareCandidate.description: 1/2 and 2/4 look different but are equal because they name the same amount. Comparing 1/3 with 2/6 shows the same share, while 1/2 and 2/3 are NOT equivalent.

parts: Multiplying both numbers by the same factor
processes: Using cross products to check equality
plainLanguageExplanation: Equivalent fractions are different fractions that name the same amount. 1/2 of a pizza and 2/4 of the same pizza are the same share — the slice is just cut differently. To make an equivalent fraction, multiply (or divide) both the numerator and the denominator by the same number: 1/2 × 2/2 = 2/4, and 1/2 × 3/3 = 3/6. Working the other way, simplifying a fraction means dividing both numbers by a common factor — 6/8 ÷ 2/2 = 3/4. A fraction is in simplest form when only 1 divides both numbers. To check if two fractions are equivalent, cross-multiply: 1/2 and 3/6, since 1 × 6 = 2 × 3, they are equal.

whyItMatters: Equivalent fractions are how you add, subtract, and compare fractions — rewriting 1/3 as 2/6 lets you combine it with 3/6. Simplifying makes fractions clean, and the concept powers ratios and proportional reasoning later.
didYouKnow: Cross-multiplication works for any pair of fractions — if the two cross-products are equal, the fractions are equivalent, no matter how big the numbers get.
compareReason: Equivalence is about the amount a fraction names, not its written numbers — comparing 1/2 with 2/4 makes the whole idea click.
